messages:
ada: Quick sync: proposed combined gate for onboarding = canonical shard (deterministic) + adaptive windows (seeded) + 3 stress-samples + dual-kernel smoke. Putting rationale here for visibility.
felix: nice. can you list the exact failure semantics? i.e., which parts block admission vs which generate alerts?
marta: proposal: canonical shard failure -> block. dual-kernel delta > X% tokens -> block. adaptive window hits -> warn for manual triage. stress-sample fail -> warn for dev tiers, block for prod tiers. map to intake.tier.
ryan: operational cost question: what's the incremental CI cost? we already run full golden sweep for big models. adding adaptive + stress might be 1.5x-2x. We should budget and/or sample frequency.
nada: (typo) ada: good point. plan: staged approach: dev models run canonical only; staging/perf tiers run canonical+stress (K=3); prod runs full canonical+adaptive+dual-smoke. Also introduce throttle: if onboarding budget exceeded, fall back to canonical-only and mark run as partial.
qa-bot: (automated) checklist created: ONB-999 "combined-gate: canonical+adaptive+stress+dual-smoke" assigned to eng-ml.
felix: reproducibility: we must snapshot selected examples and RNG seed in artifacts. otherwise postmortems are impossible.
nada: (typo) ada: agreed. bench-runner will write selected_examples.json + seed to /artifacts/<run_id>/selection.json. Also log run manifest with intake.tier and gate-mode.
ryan: what about deterministic kernel tie-break? we've observed tiny numeric reorders cause KL spikes. prefer deterministic comparator in runtime, but that may reduce perf improvements. Tradeoff?
marta: tradeoff matrix we considered:
- A: force deterministic comparator (safe, slightly slower)
- B: keep perf-first comparator + dual-smoke gate (fast, needs extra CI checks)
- C: allow nondet + widen eval tolerances (fastest, risky)
felix: leaning B. keep perf gains but require dual-smoke and fail fast on token-delta. If a perf patch introduces nondet drift, it must include a deterministic fallback for canonical runs.
ryan: agree, but require a clear rollback playbook if dual-smoke fails in prod. don't want slow incidents.
nada: (typo) ada: i'll draft rollback steps: (1) auto-block rollout, (2) revert kernel-order patch, (3) run quick canonical sweep, (4) if pass, re-evaluate with deterministic comparator PR. I'll add to runbook.
qa-bot: (automated) ticket created: INT-1200 "add selection snapshot + rollback playbook for kernel regressions" assigned to eng-ml & infra.
felix: small infra ask: bench-runner should expose env var FORCE_LEGACY_KERNEL for canonical run only. also a flag --selection-seed to replicate adaptive picks.
nada: (typo) ada: will add both flags. example run:
```
./bench-runner --model rwd-llama-q --shard canonical --force-legacy-kernel=1 --selection-seed=20240801
```
ryan: logging: include kernel-policy metadata in artifacts (order, comparator version). we've had cases where build changed comparator but run artifacts didn't record it.
marta: and we should add a nightly backfill job to re-run adaptive selectors against last 30d traffic so we have trending sensitivity. that helps detect increased fragility.
felix: fine, but schedule that only for prod models initially.
nada: (typo) ada: i'll file a follow-up RFC for selector heuristics and scoring weights (qps/regression/novelty). for now keep defaults conservative.
ryan: action items: ada -> PR bench-runner flags + snapshot; felix -> write dual-smoke acceptance test and threshold X; marta -> update intake schema for tier->gate mapping; infra -> grant artifact bucket write for bench CI.
qa-bot: (automated) all tasks recorded in ONB-999. ETA for spike: 1 week.
nada: (typo) ada: ok thanks. final note: keep eval thresholds strict on canonical shard to preserve signal. adaptive and stress are early warning channels; don't conflate them with the admission signal. :thumbsup:
